column3: The Hebrew repeats “the whole congregation of the sons of Israel.”
The Hebrew has a singular “pot of meat.”
The Hebrew says “walk in My law,” rather than simply “follow My instructions.”
The Hebrew repeats the LORD’s name in “grumbling against the LORD,” rather than using “Him.”
The Hebrew repeats the LORD’s name as the one hearing their grumbling.
The Hebrew says they “turned” toward the wilderness, rather than merely looked.
The Hebrew expression is literally “between the two evenings.”
The Hebrew says the layer of dew “went up” and repeats the description “fine.”
The Hebrew includes “according to the number of your persons” and speaks of an omer “per head.”
The Hebrew says “you will not find it,” referring to the bread, rather than “anything.”
The Hebrew addresses the people in the plural through Moses.
The Hebrew says He “is giving” bread on the sixth day, rather than “will give.”
